name: Mainz
summary: The Mainz experiment was a precision tritium beta-spectroscopy measurement of the electron-antineutrino mass. Its solid-tritium source and electrostatic spectrometer were important predecessors of KATRIN.
detection_principle: Electrons emitted by a frozen tritium source were selected by a MAC-E filter. Fits to the integrated beta spectrum close to the endpoint constrained the mass carried by the undetected antineutrino.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final phase-II analysis reported no nonzero neutrino mass and set the 2.3 eV/c2 upper limit.

collaboration.name: Mainz Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Spectrometer
key_parameters.value: Magnetic adiabatic collimation with an electrostatic filter

results.summary: The final phase-II analysis reported no nonzero neutrino mass and set the 2.3 eV/c2 upper limit.

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
